items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. Various Artists - L�ve L�ve (Volume1) (Review) Pedro Lima - Maguidala (Review) Ann O'aro - Bleu (Review)

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自丹麦三人组合 GuldGanger 的首张数字 EP，仅含五首作品。核心人物是北欧民谣圈经验丰富的歌手 Mia Guldhammer，乐手们各自带来不同视角重新诠释传统曲目。开场曲《Svennedal》节奏粗犷奔放，展示了主唱极具说服力的嗓音；唯一原创作品《Nordgård》由乐队成员 Morten Musicus 创作，口琴与风笛形成持续推进力。传统曲目《Agnete Of Bjergmanden》以扬琴营造细腻底色，末曲《Ormsö》作为器乐曲融合口琴、长笛与弦乐，产生颇具张力的偏离感。整体笼罩着古旧、略带粗粝的氛围，乐队展现出超越新秀水平的成熟度，但仍以传统民谣为根基，融合性有限。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / documentary / soundscape / social commentary
items._cn_summary: 这并非传统意义上的音乐专辑，而是录音师Ian Brennan在芝加哥南区街头录制的枪支暴力幸存者口述合集。二十五位年龄从十七岁到六十七岁的参与者来自同一街区，其中一位刚参加完追悼会，另一位正要去参加。这种口述形式强调田野录音与声音景观的真实性，背景中没有任何添加音乐，只有街道环境音。录音地点位于九十四岁祖母家前廊，正值特朗普下令国民警卫队进城的同一天。文章指出，尽管南区曾孕育Muddy Waters、Howlin' Wolf等布鲁斯传奇和Lionel Hampton等爵士大师，但这里仍是城市中被遗忘的区域。项目收益将捐给致力于以公共卫生方法遏制暴力的Cure Violence Global组织。最动人的时刻来自一位失去两个儿子、强忍泪水的老妇人反复说着"对不起"——作者认为该道歉的是社会本身。

items.album: Guest Show Report: Ken Geiger on Fricker / Evil Bong / Penis Geyser / Splooge Receptacle (Ferren Mall, New Brunswick NJ, Aug 14)
items.excerpt: August 14th was another joyous evening in New Brunswick, New Jersey, which is quickly establishing itself as a hot spot for any touring noise acts to stop through on the east coast. items.body: August 14th was another joyous evening in New Brunswick, New Jersey, which is quickly establishing itself as a hot spot for any touring noise acts to stop through on the east coast. Considering the enthusiastic attendees and diverse local talent pool available for these shows though, this comes off as no surprise. As a result, acts of both the new and old guard are able to use this intimate basement setting as a proving ground to show their stuff to a rather open-minded but critically thinking crowd. So when Midwest noisecore legends Penis Geyser announced they would be touring in celebration of their twentieth anniversary, booking them a show in Hub City was a no-brainer. First act of the night was FRICKER, who I would put into contention as modern noise’s best kept secret anywhere. The unique blend of digital soundscape smashing and crude feedback that he brings to the table can be tailored to just about any sound system that he comes across, which leads to each live experience being different from the last. Given the grimy nature of Ferren Mall’s sound system, I figured the crowd would be in for something on the crustier side of his material. Indeed, I was right on that front. Fricker spared no room for intricacies, and immediately summoned churning rumble grumble to suck the audience into a vacuum of unforgiving sound. The feedback drone that started the set eventually gave way to more variety in the chopping of digital samples, but never once lost its harsh backing. It seems like there is not a single sound system that this red-headed prince can’t conquer, and the audience seemed to think so, as much feedback I heard after was that this set made the travel and admission price alone feel worth it. With a bar set that high, things could only go up from there. When it comes to performances I take part in, I try to often gauge how the audience is feeling about things both during and after the set. With EVIL BONG, this task is never really that hard. Being showered in a sea of audience laughter and “fuck you” cries gives you a good idea of where your performance stands. With 6 members to this unit, every full band blast came closer to sounding like harsh noise wall than perhaps a noisecore band would sound. Between takes, microphone feedback would shriek like a drunken sailor beginning to hurl as song titles that took shots at New Brunswick, the audience, the bands playing and more came out of the mouth of their jackass drummer (side note: that guy really is a jerk). By the end of the set, with the audience in a frenzy, several members of the band just began to throw themselves directly at the audience. Hey, if hurting them emotionally won’t break their spirits, why not try physically?? By the time the band finished their crowd-pleasing closer, “Fuck Scronch,” there was simply nothing more they could do than to cheer and submit to the power of Evil Bong. Much like the film series this band was named after, audiences can’t help but find entertainment in the horror of this performance. To simply shower praise towards PENIS GEYSER would not be enough to describe the masterclass their performance was. While most seasoned attendees of noise shows expect short sets, nobody was expecting just 90 seconds from this touring unit. It’s 20 years of the band, you would be more than understanding if they wanted to play a long set. Nope; 90 seconds and it’s off the stage. But in that time, the band managed to whip the audience between blasting frenzy, tense restraint and dadaist rock n roll deconstruction that would have left the most seasoned of touring acts in absolute disbelief by how disciplined the trio were in their attack. While the blasting noisecore is what most of us came for, I found myself more intrigued by the moments in between, when drummer Mikeal VanCleave would gently tap on his kit while the string slinging duo of Brad Griggs and Charlie Mumma would treat their guitars as anything other than traditional songwriting. Strings were detuned, slapped around, beaten and mangled. The frenetic energy of these actions sounded closer to someone rattling their cabinet around than actually attempting to play anything musical. And when it all finally came to an end, it wasn’t bombastic. The band simply stopped playing whatever interlude they were in the midst of and started breaking their gear down. The audience cheered for an encore. I heard “One more! One more!” cried out repeatedly (what would even be “one more” for this band? Certainly not a song). Finally, one attendee walking out said “nah, it was perfect” and left. I couldn’t have said it better myself; a phenomenal band that could go on for another 20 years and probably still be as good. The new blood of New Jersey closed the evening’s happenings, as SPLOOGE RECEPTACLE came out with a table full of gear and the enthusiasm to inject their own brand of reckless abandon onto the audience. For those maybe not in the know, this group serves as the house band for New Jersey–based record label, NJMA, which has taken on the mantle of all things absurd and limited-edition in the Garden State. There are too many projects and releases to even begin listing the “essentials,” but Splooge Receptacle is where all these insane minds come together to celebrate the power of all things noise and core. Members were switching between duties on the mic, guitar, drums, electronics, etc. Really, if someone felt like they wanted to play something more than another member at the moment, they made the switch off occur. Similar to the Evil Bong performance from earlier, Splooge also engaged in their own form of audience antagonizing, as members crashed into the crowd while raging out through the wall of sound. Even when sound was not always perfect (sorry for providing a bad cable, team), their reckless abandon carried the set a great deal. With each passing set this group does, I become more and more excited at the prospect of where their sound can go. This group will be a name to look out for in the coming years if your listening diet tends to lean towards the more lo-fi ends of noisecore and shitnoise. So with the final blastbeat sounding off, the crowd took the streets, wandering off to who-the-hell-knows until the next show. Maybe some went to the nearest eatery available. Personally speaking, I went off to the Edison Diner for some late-night nachos with the Penis Geyser crew in tow. But maybe some walked away from this one thinking of how inspiring it could be to see the most chaotic and shittiest sounds performed so excellently. I know plenty that are still buzzing days later from the whole affair.

items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评记录了新泽西州新布朗斯维克一场地下噪音演出，涵盖三组表演者。FRICKER 以数字采样撕裂与粗糙反馈为核心，利用场地简陋的音响系统营造出密实的低频轰鸣与高频啸叫，强调现场不可复制的体验感。EVIL BONG 是六人编制噪音核乐队，现场以激进互动著称——观众的笑声与咒骂、麦克风反馈、攻击性歌词、以及成员直接冲撞观众的行为，将表演推向近乎行为艺术的混乱场域。PENIS GEYSER 作为中西部噪音核老将，庆祝二十周年巡演，将地下室空间转化为噪音实验的试炼场。整篇乐评侧重现场氛围与感官冲击的描述，而非音乐结构的深度分析，适合对极端地下噪音场景感兴趣的读者。

items.body: ちょっと新しいことに挑戦！ こんにちは！今回は、普段このブログで公開しているものとはちょっと違った記事になります。というか、正直に言うと、こういうことをやるのは今回が本当に初めてだったりします。 Substackの「J-Music Advance Party」8月号を読んでくださった方ならご存じかもしれませんが、そこで少しお話しした通り、記事執筆時点でのさいわいな部屋の最新アルバム『すみやかな気息』のリリースに先駆けて、ドラマーの宇都宮海さんとお話しするという、とてもありがたい機会に恵まれました。最初にバンドへ連絡したときは、ほんの一言二言でもお話を聞けたら、くらいの気持ちだったのですが、実際に返ってきたものは自分が想像していた以上のもので、これからもずっと感謝し続けるだろうなと思えるような経験になりました。 その短いやり取りの中で、ありがたいことに、アルバムについて、そしてバンドそのものについて、自分が気になっていたいくつかの質問にもメンバーのみなさんが丁寧に答えてくださいました。当初は、その回答をAdvance Partyでさいわいな部屋を紹介する際の参考にさせていただくつもりでした。 でも、実際に回答をいただいてみると、これを自分だけのところに留めて、みなさんにも共有しないのはあまりにももったいないな、と。 すでにさいわいな部屋のファンで、もっとバンドのことを知りたいと思っている方にはもちろんですが、それだけではなく、まだ彼らの音楽を知らない方にも、これをきっかけに聴いてもらえたら嬉しい。自分自身、さいわいな部屋の音楽を一人でも多くの人に知ってもらうために、できることをしたいと思ったんです。 そんなわけで、宇都宮さんに「いただいた回答をブログでも公開していいですか？」とお願いしてみたところ、ありがたいことに快くOKをいただきました。 決してものすごく長いインタビューというわけではなくて、そもそも自分でもこれを「インタビュー」と呼んでいいのかちょっと迷っているくらいなんですが（笑）、それでも、さいわいな部屋のみなさんが話してくださったことを、みなさんにも楽しんで読んでいただけたら嬉しいです。 というわけで、前置きはこのくらいにして―― さいわいな部屋とのお話を、ぜひお楽しみください！ 『すみやかな気息』について 前作の1stアルバム『すこやかな寝台』から1年半ぶりとなる、新作フルアルバムです。特別に書き留めてしまえばかえって取りこぼされてしまう、整頓されていない個人の余白や脈絡のない行動、そんな名もない営みが集まり形成された大きな集合は、ひとりでに潮流や気配を作り出し、また個人へと影響を与えます。このような循環するシステムとしての「都市」を本作のコンセプトとして据え、日常に潜むささやかな不穏さを、楽曲ごとに異なる角度から描いています。都市ど真ん中の喧騒や忙しなさに組み込まれた、人や光の呼吸を感じられるタッチを、意識して織り込んでいます。かなりのボリュームを持った作品になりましたので、じっくりと腰を据えて一曲ずつ味わいを確かめながらお聴きいただけますと幸いです。 Leap：まずアルバムについてです。『すみやかな気息』を制作するにあたって、何かテーマやコンセプトのようなものはあったのでしょうか？ 個人的な話になりますが、『すこやかな寝台』を聴いたとき、自分は「久しぶりに故郷へ帰ってきたような感覚」を覚えました。どこか安心感があって、とても居心地のいい作品だと感じています。今回のアルバムでは、リスナーに何か特定の感情や景色を思い浮かべてもらいたい、というようなイメージはありますか？ (Gt.Vo.みさ) 前作の都市郊外的な雰囲気と対比し、大きく「都市」というテーマで制作しました。そこで営まれる個人の行動や労働、それらが及ぼす相互作用のようなものを描いています。 個人的に解釈した「都市」というものを、それを形作る人のありかたや情報の回り方といった視点から歌詞に反映しています。単に記号的な都市のイメージを彷彿とさせる目的よりも、そこにある労働や人々、その相互作用など、その仕組みやある種暮らしに思いを馳せる過程を重視して書いたので、何かを読み取ろうとするよりも、聴く人もそれぞれ個人的な視点のまま何かしらを感じていただけたら嬉しいです。 Leap：また音楽的な面でも、最近Xで公開されていた試聴を聴いていて感じたのですが、新作は前作よりも全体的にテンポの速い楽曲が多い印象を受けました。自分はさいわいな部屋の、特にギターとドラムを中心としたメロディの美しさが本当に好きなのですが、『すみやかな気息』では楽器アレンジやサウンド面で何か新しい挑戦もされているのでしょうか？ (Gt.Vo.みさ) 今作では全体の統一感よりは、曲ごとの個性を際立たせるような音作りを意識しました。「インターライン」ではセミアコであえてダマっぽいギターを意識してみています。「石」では、これまでにない重めの歪んだギターサウンドやダブリングでハードな印象を与えるようにしたりしています。 (Dr.Kai Utsunomiya) ドラムについて、このバンドでは極力ドラムフレーズはシンプルに、主張しすぎないアプローチを取ろうと考えて制作しています。ですが、楽曲の個性を際立たせてバリエーションを持たせるために、前作と比べると込み入ったリズムパターンが増えているかなとは思います。確かに前作よりも曲のテンポが早いものが増えた印象はありますが、今のところ意識的に変えたつもりはありませんでした。しかし今作で「都市」というモチーフを描く際に、テンポの速い印象が結果的にプラスに作用している気はしています。むしろ今後新たに制作をする時に、今までに無い早いテンポ・新しい構成を前提として曲作りを進めていきたいなと、個人的には考えています。 (Ba. Masaya Fujimoto) 今作では前作と比べるとより3ピースにおけるベースという役割のポテンシャルを活かそうという思いを込めながら制作を進めてきました。それがより緩急を際立たせ、新たな印象を抱かせる要因の一つになっているのかなと思います。サウンド面では基本は3者のバランスを保ちつつも「誘導」では新たにオクターブエフェクトを採用していたりと密かに遊びを取り入れた作品になりました。 Leap：そして、バンドについてもぜひ少し教えていただけたら嬉しいです。さいわいな部屋はどのような経緯で結成されたのでしょうか？ (Dr.Kai Utsunomiya) 1年半ほど前に、元々私のソロプロジェクトという形でみささんに歌・ギター入れをお手伝いいただいていたことがあります。数曲一緒に作らせてもらったのですが、演奏力は言わずもがな、フレージングのセンスにも非凡なものを感じていました。こちらのソロプロジェクトは、思いついたDEMOをすぐさま形にしてどんどんリリースする方針だったので、質より量で勝負のインスタントな側面が強かったです。みささんのスキルとセンスをこの形で消費してしまうのは勿体無いと感じたため、ぜひバンドという形で新しく進めてみないかということで打診しました。 私はそのとき既にバンドをかなりの数抜けたり組んだりしてきていたので、もうこれ以上新規バンドは増やさないぞと考えてはいたのですが、泣きの一回という形で組ませてもらうことになりました。 ベースを誰にするかというところですが、みささんのスキルが卓越しているかつ私自身かなりプレーヤーのスキル面を重視するタイプなので、技術的に妥協のない人選にしたいなと僭越ながら考えていました。最初に思い当たったのが大学時代ジャズ研の先輩であったまさやさんで、正直あまりこのようなバンドで演奏しているイメージがなかったのでかなりダメもとで声をかけてみたところ、快く引き受けてくれました。1stアルバムの制作でもその圧倒的なベーススキルの片鱗が垣間見得ています。ただ、まだ彼の本領を完全に発揮できるような曲の土台作りをできていない気がしているため、これからさらにメンバーの持ち味を活かせるようなアイデア出しを進めていき、さらに「バンドらしい」制作ができている状態に持っていきたいと考えています。 Leap：また、音楽的なルーツや影響を受けたアーティストについてもお聞きしたいです。自分は、さいわいな部屋の音楽を聴いているとAmerican Footballを少し思い出す瞬間があるのですが、実際に影響を受けていたりするのでしょうか？もし他にも現在のサウンドに繋がっているバンドやアーティストがいれば、ぜひ教えていただけたら嬉しいです。 (Gt.Vo.みさ) ASIAN KUNG-FU GENERATIONとスピッツの影響は常にあります。またthe Formatが一番好きで、メロディやリフなどにキャッチーさを重要視する点としてバンド活動に限らず影響を受けていると思います。(Kai Utsunomiya)People In The BoxやChouchou merged syrups.など残響系のアーティストが好きで、制作においてリファレンスとしています。このバンドのアウトプットとしてはメンバー二人の異なる音楽的趣向と交わることでポストロックともオルタナとも言えない周辺的なジャンルを漂う結果となっており、それはある程度狙い通りであるとも言えます。 また一方、私個人としてはmidwest emoがとても好きで、ルーツとしてAmerican FootballやTTNG、ラテンアメリカやロシア、東南アジアのemoシーンからの影響をかなり受けています。メンバー二人のルーツとしては特にそのあたりのジャンルから大きな影響を受けている訳ではなさそうなものの、もらうアウトプットには近しいニュアンスが感じ取れることも多く、私主導で作る曲についてはそこを活かして制作している場合も多いかと思います。 (Ba. Masaya Fujimoto)前述の結成経緯にもある通り、自分は近年ジャズを中心とした活動をしていたため、制作活動を行う中で特定のロックバンドを意識していることはあまりなかったです。ただ、以前よく聴いていたRushからは無意識的に影響を受けている気がしますし、他ジャンルのアーティストで挙げるならば、今作はPaul JacksonやRocco Palladino、Thundercatなどからヒントを得ています。 Leap：(最後に)さいわいな部屋の音楽をご自身ではどのように表現されますか？特定のジャンルに近いという感覚があるのか、それともジャンルにとらわれない音楽だと考えているのか、そのあたりのお話もぜひ伺ってみたいです。 (Gt.Vo.みさ) 私たちの音楽は、特定のジャンルにとらわれないものだと考えています。メンバーそれぞれが異なるルーツを持っていること自体が、私たちの大きな強みです。楽曲制作の際も、あえて特定のジャンルに寄せることはしません。全員が独自の解釈でアレンジを重ねるため、時には一つのジャンルが濃く現れることも、融合することもあります。その過程で生まれる偶然性も強みの一つだと思います。 (Dr.Kai Utsunomiya) 同上で、特定のジャンルに当てはめた制作はしていません。盛り上がっているオルタナティブロックシーンの延長として語られやすい部分もあるかもしれませんが、とにかくバラエティに富んだ解釈で幅広いアプローチを試みていきたいと考えているので、スタンスとしてはポストロック的なバンドであると言いたいかもしれません。 (Ba. Masaya Fujimoto)自分もジャンルに関しては「結果」として後からラベリングされるものであって、制作においてはそれを意識することはありません。ただし、リスナーの皆さんがそれぞれ抱く「解釈」はどれも間違いではないと思うので、その解釈の余地を是非楽しんでいただければと思います。 今後も、こういうことを他のバンドやアーティストの方々とまたできたらいいなと思っています。何より、このブログでアーティストについて書くとき、自分の勝手な推測や憶測だけで語るのではなく、できる限り本人たちが思い描いているものや、その音楽に込めた考えを反映した内容にしたいと思っているからです。 それと同時に、こういった形で直接お話を聞くことも、まだ彼らのことを知らない新しいリスナーにバンドやアーティストを紹介するための、また一つの方法になるんじゃないかなとも思っています。そもそも、自分がこうして音楽について書き続けている大きな理由の一つが、それだったりするので。 ただ、改めて自分がした質問を振り返ってみると、ところどころ少し誘導的すぎたかもしれないな、とも思っています。バンドのみなさんが変なふうに感じていなければいいのですが……。こういうことは普段やっていないので、もしまた同じような機会に恵まれたら、そのあたりは自分自身もっと意識して、改善していきたいところですね。 そして、まさにその話なんですが、もしまたこういった機会を作ることができたら、今回のような「会話」をこのブログで読んでみたいか、ぜひみなさんの意見も聞かせてください！ 最後に、まだ聴いていないという方は、ぜひさいわいな部屋の最新アルバム『すみやかな気息』をチェックしてみてください！そして、バンドを応援したいという方は、ぜひCDなどのフィジカル版を手に取ることも検討してみてください。BASEとBandcampから海外発送にも対応しています。Bandcampを利用する場合は、Bandcamp Fridayに購入すると、購入代金がすべて直接バンドに還元されるということも、ぜひ覚えておいてください！ Happy Listening!
items._genre: indie rock / math rock / jangle pop
items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于日本独立摇滚乐队「さいわいな部屋」（幸福房间）专辑《すみやかな気息》的访谈式乐评。乐队以"城市"为核心概念，描绘都市中个体的劳动、行动及其相互作用的循环系统。吉他手みさ在创作中注重从人的存在方式和信息流动角度切入歌词，而非简单的城市符号。音乐制作上强调每首曲目的个性差异：使用半空心吉他营造闷哑音色、以重失真和双轨叠加制造硬朗印象、运用八度效果器等细节处理。鼓手宇都宮海追求简洁克制但变化丰富的节奏型，贝斯手藤本则着力发挥三件套编制下低频的动态潜力。整体为三人编制的日系独立摇滚作品，有一定结构意识，但与实验、前卫或电子等领域的融合并不明显。

items.body:
The legend behind Eurobeat anthem ‘Pump Up The Jam’ does folk and goth-pop in a fairly corny delivery from Stroom

After cropping up on a compilation EP (STREP-039) last year with the brooding balm of ‘Ambient Kinsky’, Jo Bogaert aka Thomas De Quincey (and tonnes more monikers) ‘fesses up to these languid and pretty cheesy cuts dating to his early years, spanning the Lemmiwinks-like strums and vox of ‘I Want You To Know Me’ and the prog-folk of ‘I Hear A Whale Song’ as part of White Light alongside Johan Guns, Kris Michiels, and Toon Vantilborgh, while the other two come from his 1983 solo album ‘None Of Them Are Green’, and follow his nose for black clad goth-rock and pop strums, including the vinegary strokes of ‘So Obscene.’
items._cn_summary: 该专辑收录了Jo Bogaert早期作品，包括与White Light合作的数首歌曲及1983年个人专辑中的曲目。音乐风格横跨民谣弹唱、前卫民谣与哥特摇滚，带有明显的复古质感和略显俗气的流行化处理。乐评指出其与Eurobeat经典曲目形成反差，展现了创作者在电子舞曲之外的多样化尝试。作品以原声吉他拨弦和演唱为主，辅以哥特暗色氛围，整体偏向轻松随性的表达，而非实验性或先锋性探索。对于关注Jo Bogaert个人历史或喜欢复古民谣与暗潮结合听感的听众，这张合辑提供了了解其早期创作脉络的窗口。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑源自一件生成式声音装置作品，素材来自人声处理、田野录音与持续低音。创作者通过程序化生成手段，将语言碎片与环境声响解构重组，探讨意义如何在不同的交流媒介间发生位移与变形。声音设计偏向极简与持续性，强调空间感与聆听过程中的时间流动。文中未提供更多具体细节，但从有限的描述来看，这是一种介于装置艺术与声音作品之间的实验性尝试，与传统器乐或作曲路径明显不同。专辑整体倾向于在安静的音场中放置大量细节等待被发现，适合开放性聆听与沉浸式体验。对关注声音艺术、田野录音、生成音乐与极简主义聆听的听众而言，这样的创作方向具有一定的吸引力。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — WARNING: This is a release of material recorded in 1972 that represents two different bands containing some of the same musicians that just happen to overlap in that year.Recorded 1972, unreleased until 1999. I was turned on to Riff Raff a few weeks ago so I've been slowly getting to know their music and their story. I was immediately impressed (and astounded that I'd never heard of them--even in my 18 years associated with ProgArchives) by all of their albums--which made the decision of which album to review first very difficult since, in learning their story I'd discovered that their first records--their debut album--had never been released at the time of its creation. But I do like to get to know a band/artist in chronological order if I can, so, of course I want to start with their first album: the problem is that their first album that became known to the public was their second album, the eponymously titled Riff Raff from 1973; Outside Looking In never reached public ears until 1999! As I've been listening to this album I've come to know that the opening 39 minutes represent material performed by the band's original lineup, a project calling themselves, STRABISMUS, which recorded this material in London in 1972. The second 23-minutes of "Bonus Tracks" represents Roger Sutton and Tommy Eyre's more-Jazz-oriented band, RIFF RAFF. Sutton, himself a former member of Brian Auger's Trinity project, continued to develop Riff Raff for the next few years with keyboardist Tommy Eyre, guitarist Peter Kirtley, and drummer Aureo De Souza before giving himself completely to Ian Carr's NUCLEUS. Peter Kirtley's most notable credit post-Riff Raff was his contribution to an album that has always remained dear to me: Yes' Alan White's first solo album, 1976's Ramshackled., while also joining The Pentangle during their tenure in the 1990s. Tommy Eyre himself was a product of previous collaborations with Aynsley Dunbar and Mark-Almond. He would go on to make significant contributions to successful albums by Zzebra, Alex Harvey, Gerry Rafferty, Gary Moore, John Martyn, Greg Lake, Michael Schenker, and Wham!. Singer Alan Marshall was hired by Zzebra (at the suggestion of the band's newcomer keyboard player, Tommy Eyre) as their singer for the 1974-75 sessions and tour that would produce the material for the band's classic sophomore album, Panic, as well as a third and fourth album--which weren't released until 1999 and 2001, respectively. Brasilian-born percussionist/drummer Aureo De Souza would also find himself hired by Ian Carr, as a percussionist, for Nucleus' mid-70s classic funk albums, but the material he recorded with the band never reached the public as part of their studio album releases--only surfaced years later (mostly in the 21st Century) when record labels Vertigo, Andy Gray's BGO (Beat Goes On) Records, and Esoteric Recordings began releasing retrospective CDs that included outtakes and live performances.Line-up / Musicians:As STRABISMUS:- Alan Marshall / vocals- Martin Ball / guitar- Tommy Eyre / Hammond organ, keyboards, acoustic guitar- Richie Dalton / saxophone- Roger Sutton (Brian Auger's Trinity) / bass, acoustic guitars, vocals- Rob Coombes (Juicy Lucy, Stealers Wheel) / drums, percussion & acoustic guitar- Joe Peters (Jackie Jocko) / drumsAs RIFF RAFF:- Alan Marshall / vocals- Peter Kirtley / guitar- Kenny Slade (Joe Cocker) / drums- Aureo De Souza / drums, percussion- Tommy Eyre / Hammond organ, keyboards, acoustic guitar- Richie Dalton / saxophone- Roger Sutton / bass, acoustic guitars, vocals(As Strabismus):1. "Outside Looking In" (9:12) opening a debut album with a long-playing jam is bold and brave! I guess it lets the listener know what kind of band they thought of themselves (unless the song order was altered over time or never decided at the time of its first creation): not hit makers. The material here is heavy, fully Rock 'n' Roll with some creative touches, nice construction and delivery, more akin to hard rockin' guitar-jammin' bands like Cream, Spirit, Mountain, Humble Pie, etc. (18.125/20)2. "The Blind Man" (8:16) opens with a much more acoustic orientation: bluesy piano, percussion and drums, Hammond organ, acoustic guitars, and vocals from a gravelly-voiced male singer. I'm immediately reminded of Southern Rock bands like The Allman Brothers and The Marshall Tucker Band. The cessation of the vocal leads into a rockin' jam with saxophonist Richie Dalton really letting loose with some wild screaming sounds. But then there is this totally unexpected transition around the five-minute mark into a more delicate, almost folk-Mexican acoustic guitar motif in which I believe four of the band members drop their instruments to pick up acoustic guitars and then what sounds like professional choral singers join in singing "Close your eyes, I can feel you" over and over before Alan rejoins to sing over them to the song's close. Very cool and unexpected song and music. (18.25/20)3. "Bach B. Minor Prelude" (2:58) a full solo on a church organ! Luscious! Another very cool and unexpected song. (9/10)4. "Feeling Paranoic" (0:43) a theatric song that feels like an outtake from Judas' or Jesus' performances in Jesus Christ Superstar. (4.375/5)5. "Buthelezi" (3:42) drummer Joe Peters leads the way through a drum & percussion jam that involves Rob Coombes and others. I love this kind of stuff--especially in live performances (or to participate in) but I'm not sure of its place on a studio album: it seems as if this space could/should have been given to a proper full-band song composition. But then I'm beginning to wonder if there is a conceptual theme, intention, or organization to the album. Anyone? (9/10)6. "So You Want To Be Free" (10:52) the music here is a return to the raw hard rock that we encountered with the album's opening song, "Outside Looking In." The raw, gravelly voice of Alan Marshall is back up front for the first couple minutes, then the music transitions into a vamp governed by a quick three-note riff that is repeated over and over while everyone just jams over and around it: saxophone, electric piano, drums, even, eventually, electric guitar. The sax solo is the best of the three; guitarist Martin Ball is not "fully formed" yet though he does sound better once the vamp slows down and punctuates itself like some Swamp Blues and he starts shredding for speed. (I guess he needed to get warmed up.) Martin's solo section ends with some well-timed whole-band chord bashing which sounds really cool and inventive--like something King Crimsonian--but then the music turns to smoother blues rock over which two male vocalists sing, gentler, harmonizing, before the music begins to slowly devolve into just a few percussion/cymbal noises and guitar and electric piano notes. Brilliant--and so creative! (18.25/20)7. "Changes" (3:23) acoustic guitar accompanying Alan's singing on what sounds like a cover but apparently is just another of the album's Sutton/Coombes compositions. Simple and nice; definitely could have been developed into something bigger. (8.667/10)Total time: 39:06A-/4.5 stars; a near-masterpiece of eclectic Southern Power Rock.Bonus Tracks (as Riff Raff):8. "Child Of The Summer" (5:59) a jazzy feeling song with a syncopated, complex construction and feeling vocal performance (reminiscent of Allan's performance on Allan White's Ramshakled). After the chorus the band revs up and becomes more rock-forceful--but it's still good! Nice wah-wah-ed electric guitar work, great background vocal work, great dirty electric piano, and awesome bass, drums, and percussion at the base. This is the rock-perspective to Jazz-Rock Fusion that I've been hoping to find more of! (9.25/10)9. "For Every Dog" (4:05) a truly awesome acoustic Southern Rock song that should/could've been a radio-friendly hit back in 1973. Great weave of instrumental performances blessed with a weave of awesome group harmonized vocals. Shades of The Youngbloods, Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young, Ozark Mountain Daredevils, Pure Prairie League, or the early Doobie Brothers or Eagles. (9.5/10)10. "Morning" (5:57) piano-based soft bluesy light folk/Americana pop arranged with an odd triple-hop at the end of each measure. The singer is mostly backed by another harmonizing vocalist (or vocal track) while acoustic guitars, bass, and gentle drums back/accompany the piano and singers. I believe a flute may also be in the mix though its replication of the piano's legato may be just be a second piano track. A very pleasant, not-quite-Cat Stevens, not-quite-Harry Nilsson tune. (8.875/10)11. "The Garden" (6:59) bluesy solo piano opens this for about 30 seconds before Allan and the background choir vocalists join in. The song sounds almost like a church/liturgical piece--something one might hear in the countryside villages of Ireland. Strummed 12-string acoustic guitar, bass, congas, and drums slowly, almost surreptitiously, join in as Allan gives his hear and soul to his vocal performance. There is definitely a flute in this one--entering just before the piano ramps things up with more volume. There is a little Dave Mason "We Just Disagree" sound and feel here. Then Allan really brings it: belting out with two minutes to go but then things quickly de-escalate as he and his backing singers sing softly about the importance of our ancestor/elders. It drags on a bit but it's a very nice song with a great vocal performance and some nice, positive lyrics. (13.375/15)Total time: 24:00A-/five stars; a minor masterpiece of Jazz- and Rock-informed Southern Folk Rock.Total Time: 62:06 I don't usually review "bonus" material in my album reviews (because I want to treat the material as it would have been heard in the year it was recorded) but then when this was (finally) released in 1999 it arrived in CD format and, thus, being its first exposure to the public, should be heard as a whole. The problem, of course, comes with the fact that the material is really the result of two completely different bands: one that never really persisted, the other which came out and toured for a year or so before scattering its members across the musical spectrum in the UK and US. I definitely like both "albums" though the Riff Raff "bonus" material is more of the kind of stuff that I'd listen to over and over. (I almost want to rate the two "albums" separately! A-/five stars; a minor masterpiece of Jazz-infused Southern Folk Rock.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑实为1972年录制、1999年才公开的两支乐队合集。前39分钟由原始阵容Strabismus在伦敦录制的作品构成，后23分钟则是更偏向爵士风格的Riff Raff乐队的曲目。乐评并未对音乐本身进行深入分析，而是花费大量篇幅梳理乐队成员的历史脉络：贝斯手Roger Sutton曾参与Brian Auger的Trinity计划，后加入Ian Carr的Nucleus；键盘手Tommy Eyre横跨Zzebra、Alex Harvey、Gerry Rafferty、Wham!等众多乐队；吉他手Peter Kirtley参与了Alan White的首张个人专辑。打击乐手Aureo De Souza同样后来服务于Nucleus。这张合集的价值更多体现在历史文献层面——它是了解70年代英国爵士摇滚场景中一支被忽视乐队的重要窗口，填补了ProgArchives听众的认知空白。作为1999年的遗作发行，其音乐内容本身在评论中并未获得充分评述。

items._cn_summary: 这是一期名为《Race The Sky》的电台节目，主持人Cliff Furnald以海藻作为主题线索，串联起来自欧洲、亚洲、南北美洲以及未知地域的音乐片段。节目自我定位为'保证无类型限制'，意在打破流派边界，展现跨文化的音乐探索。从描述来看，该节目涵盖了世界音乐与实验性元素的融合，涉及多个大洲的音乐传统。RootsWorld是一个专注于世界音乐与跨文化音乐的小众平台，具有一定的策展视野。然而原文内容极为简短，仅为节目简介，未提供具体音乐作品、艺术家或音乐特征的分析，信息量严重不足，难以深入评估其音乐品质与艺术价值。作为一档展示多元文化的电台节目，对世界音乐爱好者有一定参考意义。

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.
Tiny Sun -
Vanishment
(Review)
Carolina Chocolate Drops -
Genuine Negro Jig
(Review)

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items._cn_summary: 这张现场专辑录制于1999年德国洛雷莱露天剧场，记录了Dr. John与新奥尔良乐手在莱茵河畔的演出。演出以Mardi Gras巡演形式呈现，混合新奥尔良经典曲目与个人创作。开场的'Iko Iko'带有半唱半诵的社区参与感，'I Walk on Guilded Splinters'展现Night Tripper式的迷幻funk风格，加入丛林音效与怪诞滑哨声。'Qualified'以放克律动表达强硬态度，'Right Place, Wrong Time'是其知名代表作。乐队编制紧凑，吉他、贝斯与鼓的组合推动现场节奏。Dr. John本人身兼歌手、钢琴与吉他，将新奥尔良传统funk、blues与巫毒仪式意象贯穿全程，尾声'Earl King的Big Chief'以Mardi Gras式狂热收尾。整体虽具地域文化色彩，但风格偏向传统funk与R&B演绎，与实验性或前卫方向关联有限。

items.body: Dwayne Goettel, keyboardist, sampling and programming specialist for the industrial band Skinny Puppy, died on 23 August 1995 at the age of 31. He was found dead at his parents’ home in Edmonton, Alberta, of an apparent heroin overdose. Thirty-one years on, Goettel remains one of the defining figures behind Skinny Puppy’s sound between 1986 and 1995. Dwayne Rudolph Goettel was born on 1 February 1964 in High Prairie, Alberta, Canada. A classically trained pianist, he grew up in Edmonton, where he played trumpet in his high school band before taking up piano and getting involved in the city’s small electronic music scene, including the groups Psyche and Water. He met cEvin Key in 1985 when Water opened for Skinny Puppy on their “Bites” tour. Key asked him to join the band the following year, replacing keyboardist Bill Leeb, who left to form Front Line Assembly. Goettel made his first contributions to Skinny Puppy on the album “Mind: The Perpetual Intercourse” (1986). His technical knowledge of samplers and studio equipment, particularly the Ensoniq Mirage, helped steer the band away from its early synth-pop sound toward the more abrasive, sample-driven style of “Cleanse Fold and Manipulate” (1987), “VIVIsectVI” (1988), “Rabies” (1989), “Too Dark Park” (1990) and “Last Rights” (1992). cEvin Key later credited Goettel’s early command of the technology, calling him “the master of sampling.” Alongside his work with Skinny Puppy, Goettel collaborated with Key on the side projects The Tear Garden, formed with singer Edward Ka-Spel, as well as Doubting Thomas, Hilt and Cyberaktif, which Key also shared with Bill Leeb. Goettel released solo material under the name aDuck and, in 1993, co-founded the label Subconscious Communications with Phil Western. Skinny Puppy’s eighth studio album, “The Process,” was recorded in Los Angeles beginning in 1993, but the sessions were marked by drug problems and conflict within the band. Vocalist Nivek Ogre quit in June 1995, and Goettel and Key returned to Vancouver with the master tapes. Goettel entered a rehabilitation programme in Edmonton before returning to work on Download, a side project he had started with Key. He was later readmitted to rehab. On 23 August 1995, Goettel was found dead at his parents’ home in Edmonton; his death was attributed to a heroin overdose. “The Process” was completed by Key and producer Dave “Rave” Ogilvie and released in 1996, dedicated to Goettel’s memory, as was Download’s debut album, “Furnace.” About Skinny Puppy Skinny Puppy formed in Vancouver, Canada, in 1982 as a side project for cEvin Key (born Kevin Crompton), who was also drumming in the new wave band Images in Vogue. Key recruited Nivek Ogre (Kevin Ogilvie) as vocalist, and the pair adopted stage names to avoid confusion between two members both named Kevin. The band self-released the EP “Back & Forth” in 1983 and signed to Vancouver label Nettwerk the same year. The EP “Remission” followed in December 1984, and Skinny Puppy’s debut full-length album, “Bites,” arrived in 1985. Bill Leeb, performing as Wilhelm Schroeder, joined on bass synth and backing vocals during this period. Leeb left the band in 1986 to form Front Line Assembly, and Dwayne Goettel replaced him, making his first contributions to “Mind: The Perpetual Intercourse” (1986). Skinny Puppy went on to release “Cleanse Fold and Manipulate” (1987), “VIVIsectVI” (1988) and “Rabies” (1989), the last featuring Ministry’s Al Jourgensen, followed by “Too Dark Park” (1990) and “Last Rights” (1992), the band’s final album for Nettwerk. In 1993 the group signed to Rick Rubin’s American Recordings and relocated to Los Angeles to record “The Process.” The sessions were affected by conflict and drug problems; Ogre quit in June 1995, and Goettel died two months later. Key and Dave “Rave” Ogilvie completed “The Process,” releasing it in 1996 in Goettel’s memory. Skinny Puppy reunited for a one-off performance at the Doomsday Festival in Dresden, Germany, in August 2000, leaving the keyboard station on stage empty in tribute to Goettel. The band reformed as a full-time project in 2003 with producer Mark Walk, releasing “The Greater Wrong of the Right” (2004), “Mythmaker” (2007), “HanDover” (2011) and “Weapon” (2013). In a 2023 interview, the band confirmed it had split up for good after more than four decades together. Goettel’s death on 23 August 1995 remains part of that history: 31 years on, his contribution to albums including “Too Dark Park” and “Last Rights” is remembered as central to Skinny Puppy’s sound.
items._cn_summary: 本文并非音乐评论，而是一篇纪念Skinny Puppy键盘手Dwayne Goettel逝世31周年的传记式新闻稿。文章详细回顾了他的生平：出生于加拿大阿尔伯塔省，接受古典钢琴训练后转向电子音乐场景，加入Skinny Puppy后凭借对Ensoniq Mirage采样器的精通，将乐队从早期合成器流行风格引向更具攻击性、以采样为核心的声音方向，参与了《Cleanse Fold and Manipulate》《VIVIsectVI》《Too Dark Park》等多张经典专辑的制作。他还与cEvin Key合作了The Tear Garden等多个侧支项目，并共同创立了Subconscious Communications厂牌。文章末尾对其参与的《The Process》录制期间乐队内部的药物问题与冲突进行了记述，但未对音乐本身进行任何艺术性评价或分析。

items.body: Front 242 released the album “05:22:09:12 Off” on 23 August 1993 through Red Rhino Europe, with Epic issuing the record in the United States that November. The seventh studio album by the Belgian industrial/EBM group turns 33 this year. Its title is a substitution cipher spelling out the word “evil,” each letter replaced by its position in the alphabet. “05:22:09:12 Off” was produced and mixed by Daniel Bressanutti and Patrick Codenys alongside John Dubs and Eran Westwood, with Bob Ludwig mastering. The album marks the only Front 242 studio release built primarily around a guest vocalist: Kristin “99” Kowalski of the New York band Spill sings lead on most tracks, with Jean-Luc De Meyer appearing only on the remix “Melt (Again).” The CD edition runs 16 tracks, including “Animal (Cage),” “Modern Angel,” “Junkdrome,” “Serial Killers Don’t Kill Their Girlfriend,” “GenEcide” and “Crushed.” The album reached number 27 on the CMJ Radio Top 150. About Front 242 Front 242 formed in 1981 in Aarschot, near Leuven, Belgium, founded by Daniel Bressanutti (electronics, production) and Dirk Bergen (graphic design). Patrick Codenys (keyboards, programming) and vocalist Jean-Luc De Meyer joined in 1982, and Richard “23” Jonckheere (electronic percussion, backing vocals) joined in 1983 as Bergen moved into design and management. The band’s 1984 album “No Comment” was among the first releases to use the term “electronic body music” in its liner notes. Front 242 signed to Wax Trax! in the US in 1984, then released “Official Version” (1987) and “Front by Front” (1988) via Red Rhino Europe/PIAS, and “Tyranny (For You)” (1991) via Epic, its highest-charting album in the US. “05:22:09:12 Off” followed in 1993, released in Europe by Red Rhino Europe on 23 August and in the US by Epic that November. Drummer Tim Kroker joined for live performances in 2008. The band’s most recent studio album, “Pulse,” followed via XIII Bis/Metropolis in 2003. In 2023, Front 242 co-headlined the “Join The Forces” tour of Europe with Nitzer Ebb, alternating headline sets across dates including Berlin, Amsterdam, Oslo and Munich. Front 242 announced its farewell “Black Out” tour in March 2024 and played its final three shows at Ancienne Belgique in Brussels on 23-25 January 2025, retiring from live performance with a lineup of Bressanutti, De Meyer, Codenys, Richard 23 and Kroker. The live album “Black Out”, drawn from more than forty farewell-tour shows, followed via Alfa Matrix on 19 June 2026. “05:22:09:12 Off” now marks 33 years since its original release.
items._cn_summary: 本文并非原创乐评，而是比利时工业/EBM团体Front 242第七张录音室专辑发行33周年的纪念性新闻稿。文章介绍了该专辑的基本信息：1993年8月由Red Rhino Europe发行、Epic在美国发行的历史，标题是以字母在字母表中位置替换拼写'evil'的密码学手法，制作人为Bressanutti与Codenys，特别之处在于这是乐队唯一一张以客座主唱Kristin Kowalski为主的专辑，曲目包括Animal (Cage)、Modern Angel、Junkdrome等16首。文章还简述了乐队自1981年成立至今的历史脉络，包括签约Wax Trax!与Epic的历程、2024年告别巡演及2025年最终演出等信息。内容为事实性陈述，缺乏对音乐本体、制作手法或艺术价值的分析评论。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — A year after forming and recording the Strabismus material in 1972 as well as the initial Riff Raff material (which would not see the light of day until 1999), Roger Sutton is trying again: this time with veterans Peter Kirtley, Tommy Eyre, Brasilian percussionist Aureo De Souza, and Bud Beadle, one of Ian Carr's partners in crime, on saxophones.1. "Your World" (7:39) a gorgeous little 12-string guitar based song with some great vocals from guitarist Peter Kirtley turns to blues-proggy Rock 'n' Roll in the third minute, getting heavier until fully-breaking out into some awesome prog rock in the fourth minute followed by a wonderful slightly-funky Fender Rhodes based Blues-Rock instrumental passage in the fifth over which Peter then turns his significant talent to his electric guitar, delivering an awesome lightly wah-wah-ed solo for almost two minutes. Then the music thins and acoustic guitar and Rhodes rebuild while the lead vocalist ramps things up to reveal a more raspy voice in his impassioned state. But the band softens back up for the final minute, even sporting some gorgeous AMERICA-like harmony vocals to close it out. Wow! I am humbled--and impressed! (14.5/15)2. "For Every Dog" (3:46) a very different version than the one the band had recorded for their original debut record (which never saw the light of day until 1999): this one is much thinner, more stark and open as opposed to the brilliantly layered weaves (both instrumental and vocal) of the original. It's still good but there is no doubt that I prefer the Allan Marshall-fronted version. (8.75/10)3. "Little Miss Drag" (3:12) sounds and plays out like a "new" Beatles tune. Even the sound production is rather like the preferences that John Lennon used in his solo career--even the snarkiness of lyrics have Lennon written all over them! (The songwriting credit cites Sutton and non-members Tony Thorpe and John Richardson as the composers--possibly/probably friends of Roger's.) (8.875/10)4. "Dreaming" (4:32) a two part song that starts out rather innocuously with gentle Fender Rhodes, bass, organ, and cymbal play for the first half minute before Peter's twangy lead electric guitar supplies a Countrified melody before the band cuts back to nothing. Then they slowly build back up while a gentle male vocal sings with an almost insecure vulnerability. Then, at the two-minute mark strummed guitars, jazz piano, hand percussion, and bass launch into a delightfully smooth-yet-spirited two-chord vamp over which Bud's saxophone and Peter's electric guitar play a "solo" melody line as a twin-duo. Really engaging, pretty and fun. (9.25/10)5. "Times Lost" (4:15) another gentle multiple picked acoustic guitar weave with one very gentle, sensitive, almost breathy male voice singing to mimick the Right channel's guitar's treble melody line. I like Roger's fretless bass work here. Nice song though I would never call this Jazz, Rock or even Folk; it's more like acoustic Folk Rock. (9.125/10)6. "You Must Be Joking" (7:29) Jazzy Blues Rock?! Using some DOORS sounds and tricks, the music gradually ramps up into a kind of Jazz-Rock as guitar, keys, and saxophone tracks weave together some pretty intricate riffs and legato lines. Peter Kirtley's lyrics and voice again have an interesting John Lennon-like snark and cleverness while, as said, the Fender Rhodes-based four chord music seems to borrow from The Doors as well as early Who and even Van Morrison. Peter's lead guitar solo in the fourth minute (over some excellent drumming from Aureo) is pretty awesome: definitely deserving of repeated listens and study. (Why did this dude never really make it to the top?) Then comes a stripped down passage within which Tommy Eyre lays down some nice keyboard work with his dirty Rhodes before closing things down by tapering off into . . . silence. (13.75/15)7. "La M�me Chose" (12:12) dreamy Rhodes play with bass, cymbals, and saxophone floating around, trying to figure out their places within the Cosmos. In the third minute Tommy's Rhodes assembles a little momentum, slowly joined by Roger's bass, Aureo's drums, and Peter's rhythm guitar--which eventually become high-tension power chords over which he and the boys sing with some confidence and fire. A slow down in the fifth minute leads into an Allman Brothers-like section, which then ramps back up into the more intense power Folk Rock motif for single- and multiple voice singing. Then, in the seventh minute, things slow back down and thin out with active bass and steady cymbal and rhythm guitar play supporting Tommy's heavily treated Rhodes solo. It's a long solo with every one amping up the further we get into it, but Tommy remaining in the spotlight, taking every second for all he's worth. Bob joins in toward the end to take the volume over the top, causing Tommy to relinquish his lead (and momentum) which then allows Bob a turn in the lead, following the same slow build as they did with Tommy, until guitar power chords take back over as the lead singer returns to declare the song's meaningful intentions before everybody goes into slow decay for the finish. Nice tune! I really love the way the band orchestrates the tension levels throughout--easily and effectively transferring it to we, the listener. (22.5/25)Total Time: 43:05I think it's the prominent acoustic guitars and pleasant, easy-going voices of Roger, Peter, and Tommy that surprise me the most about this album--that and the sophisticated, creative, and confident songwriting.A-/five stars; another minor masterpiece of little-mentioned, perhaps forgotten, song-crafting by some truly excellent and creative songwriters and musicians. Definitely the product of professionals who know what they're doing (and seem to have a strongly defined vision for their music). This may not be as proggy as the Top Tier (mostly symphonic) bands, but it is very high quality music.
items._cn_summary: 这张1973年的专辑由贝斯手Roger Sutton领衔，集合了吉他手Peter Kirtley、键盘手Tommy Eyre、巴西打击乐手Aureo De Souza以及Ian Carr的合作伙伴Bud Beadle担任萨克斯手。乐评对开篇曲给予了极高评价，认为它从十二弦吉他民谣出发，逐步过渡到蓝调摇滚、前卫摇滚段落，并以芬达Rhodes电钢琴为基础的放克器乐段展开，结尾呈现近似America式的和声。评论特别提及了Peter Kirtley的人声与吉他演奏，以及Roger的无品贝斯技巧。专辑被定位为爵士摇滚融合，但乐评在最后一曲中明确指出某些作品更接近原声民谣而非爵士或摇滚。整体而言，这张专辑在编曲上展现出一定的层次感和融合意图，但风格上偏向传统的前卫摇滚与爵士摇滚结合，与实验、前卫或即兴的核心方向存在距离。

items.body: Depeche Mode, the English electronic band from Basildon, Essex, released “Construction Time Again” on 22 August 1983 through Mute Records. The album turns 43 this year. It was the band’s third studio album and reached number 6 on the UK Albums Chart. Daniel Miller produced the album together with Depeche Mode, with Gareth Jones engineering. Recording took place at the Garden studio in London, mixing at Hansa Mischraum in Berlin, and mastering at CBS Studios in London. The band built much of the album around sampled found sounds, recorded on a Synclavier and an Emulator, including metal being struck and other industrial noises. “Construction Time Again” was the first Depeche Mode studio album to feature Alan Wilder as a full member; he co-wrote two of the album’s songs. The nine-track album runs “Love, in Itself,” “More Than a Party,” “Pipeline,” “Everything Counts,” “Two Minute Warning,” “Shame,” “The Landscape Is Changing,” “Told You So” and “And Then…” Mute released “Everything Counts” as the lead single on 11 July 1983, ahead of the album; it reached number 6 on the UK Singles Chart. “Love, in Itself” followed as the second single on 19 September 1983 and peaked at number 21. “Construction Time Again” followed “A Broken Frame” (1982) and preceded “Some Great Reward” (1984), the album that produced “People Are People.” About Depeche Mode Vince Clarke, Martin Gore, Dave Gahan and Andy Fletcher formed Depeche Mode in Basildon, Essex, in 1980, taking their name from a French fashion magazine. The band signed to Daniel Miller’s independent label Mute Records and released the synth-pop debut album “Speak & Spell” in 1981. Clarke left the band after that album to form Yazoo with Alison Moyet, and Gore took over as the band’s main songwriter. Depeche Mode continued as a trio for “A Broken Frame” (1982), then expanded to a four-piece with the addition of Alan Wilder for “Construction Time Again” (1983), the album that introduced sampled industrial sounds and engineer Gareth Jones to the band’s productions. The Miller and Jones production team continued with Depeche Mode through “Some Great Reward” (1984), “Black Celebration” (1986), “Music for the Masses” (1987) and “Violator” (1990), the album that produced “Personal Jesus” and “Enjoy the Silence.” Wilder left the band in 1995 after “Songs of Faith and Devotion” (1993); Depeche Mode continued as a trio of Gahan, Gore and Fletcher, releasing “Ultra” (1997), “Exciter” (2001), “Playing the Angel” (2005), “Sounds of the Universe” (2009), “Delta Machine” (2013) and “Spirit” (2017). Fletcher died in May 2022, and Gahan and Gore released “Memento Mori” as a duo in 2023, touring behind a Mexico City concert film titled “M.” “Construction Time Again,” released 22 August 1983, marked the start of the band’s move from straightforward synth-pop toward the denser, sample-driven productions that shaped its subsequent albums.
items._cn_summary: 文章以纪念性质回顾Depeche Mode 1983年专辑《Construction Time Again》发行43周年。内容主要为新闻式信息整理，涵盖专辑制作背景、曲目列表、唱片成绩以及乐队成员变动与厂牌合作历史。该专辑是乐队首次大量采用采样环境声响（金属撞击、工业噪音）作为创作素材，通过Synclavier与Emulator进行声音构建，Alan Wilder也以正式成员身份首次参与制作。制作团队Daniel Miller与Gareth Jones的合作延续至后续多张重要专辑。整体而言，文章属于资讯性回顾，缺乏对音乐本身的深度评论或艺术性分析，更偏向编年史式的资料整理而非真正意义上的乐评。

items.body: German EBM and electro label emmobiz records releases “V.A. 19. Elektrisch Festival” on 24 October 2026, the same day as the 19th Elektrisch Festival at Club Seilerstraße in Zwickau. The 10-inch is pressed on brown vinyl, limited to 222 copies, and sells for 16.99 euro through the label’s own shop. Six tracks from five acts fill the two sides. The record continues an annual series that the label has run since the festival returned in 2024, following the red-vinyl 16th edition and the 17th edition 10-inch, and the 18th, which split across an EBM Edition and a Synth Pop Edition earlier this year. emmobiz describes the Elektrisch series as the only festival compilation of its kind carrying rare or exclusive tracks from the acts on the bill. What is on the 19. Elektrisch Festival 10-inch Four of the five acts on the record play the festival. Portion Control, this year’s headliner, does not appear on the compilation. The label fills the gap with two bonus tracks by acts outside the bill. A1: Escalator, “Utolsókor (Short)”, 3:47 A2: Oszylayter, “we’re the noise”, 4:01 A3: Cyborg Projekt X, “Native Terror” (Vinyl Edit), 3:49 B1: Krieg-B, “kill the light” (V111 Mix), 5:20 B2: Sabotage Q.C.Q.C., “Heidenangst” (Drumatic), 6:05 B3: TöT, “Diers Irae” (Rough Mix), 2:27 The two bonus cuts on the B-side reach outside the festival line-up. Sabotage Q.C.Q.C. are a German electro act who released through Spin Records and EMI Electrola in the 1990s; “Heidenangst” first appeared on their 1996 album “Sexploitation Cinema” and returned in remixed form on the 1997 maxi-single “Schlager”. The version here is a new remake made for this record. Closing the compilation, the Marseille electro-punk and EBM band TöT contribute “Diers Irae”. Escalator, the Budapest EBM band founded in 1988 by 2RT+TB, took their starting point from Kraftwerk and have released since 1989. Oszylayter bring electropunk and breakbeat from Germany. Krieg-B, the Franco-Belgian project Dominique Lallement and Benoît Buyse started in June 2023, follow their emmobiz debut “War Drums’ Resonance” with the album “Concrete Dominion”, which the label also dates to 24 October. About the Elektrisch Festival and emmobiz records The Elektrisch Festival ran five editions in Zwickau between 2007 and 2010, from the 11th to the 15th, at the city’s BPM Club. It then stopped for 14 years. emmobiz records brought it back in 2024 with the 16th edition at Club Seilerstraße, which sold out in advance behind Calva Y Nada, Cat Rapes Dog, Digital Factor and Accessory. The 17th followed in October 2025 and the 18th ran over two evenings in February 2026. The 19th takes place on 24 October 2026 with Portion Control, Escalator, Oszylayter, Cyborg Projekt X and Krieg-B; doors open at 19:00 and the music starts at 20:00. emmobiz records is run by Jörg Freier from Oelsnitz in the Erzgebirge, Saxony, and specialises in industrial, EBM and synthpop. The label stopped operating at the end of 2017 and relaunched on 22 August 2024 with a vinyl reissue of Tyske Ludder’s “Bombt Die Mörder?”. Since then it has reissued the Calva Y Nada catalogue on picture disc, pressed Apoptygma Berzerk’s “Kathy’s Song XXV”, and put out records by Second Decay, Blind Passengers, Fairlight Children and Piston Damp. It organises the festival as well as documenting it, and the 10-inch goes on sale the day the doors open.
items._cn_summary: 这是德国厂牌emmobiz records为第19届Elektrisch Festival发行的限量10寸黑胶合集，棕色唱片压制222张，售价16.99欧元，收录五组艺人的六首作品。内容以电波EBM和electro风格为主，包括Escalator的Utolsókor短曲版、Oszylayter的we're the noise、Cyborg Projekt X的Native Terror等。B面附赠两首非演出阵容曲目：Sabotage Q.C.Q.C.重新制作的Heidenangst及马赛乐队TöT的Diers Irae。整篇文章更偏向音乐节与厂牌的资讯性介绍，缺乏对音乐本身的深入分析与艺术评价，文字内容截断于厂牌介绍部分。

items.album: I Ya Toyah releases Nine Inch Nails cover ‘Closer’ on Femme Fatale Records

items.body: Chicago industrial and darkwave artist I Ya Toyah released “Closer”, a cover of the Nine Inch Nails song, on 21 August 2026 through her own label Femme Fatale Records. It is a digital single, and it arrives with a video the same week. On Bandcamp the artist describes the release in a single line: “This is the cover of Nine Inch Nail’s song.” Closer by I Ya Toyah The original was written by Michael Trent Reznor and appeared on Nine Inch Nails‘ 1994 album “The Downward Spiral”. I Ya Toyah produced this version with Johnny K, who also mixed it. Howie Weinberg mastered the track and Angelica Dulany supplied the artwork. Publishing runs through Leaving Hope Music and TVT Music, with the cover licensed through Easy Song Licensing. “Closer” is the third single I Ya Toyah has issued through Femme Fatale Records this year, after the two-track “Feelings” on 1 May and “Apology” on 26 June. Johnny K mixed and produced all three, and Howie Weinberg mastered them. Her press release describes the run as a completed trilogy about the forces that shape identity. The ‘Closer’ video The video was filmed and directed by Alex Zarek, who edited it with I Ya Toyah. The concept is hers. Angelica Dulany handled production assistance and additional direction, Janet Debris did makeup and Allison Ciletti managed the location. It went up on her own YouTube channel on 21 August 2026. The single is on Bandcamp and on the usual streaming services through a single smart link. About I Ya Toyah I Ya Toyah is the solo project of Ania Tarnowska, a Polish-born musician, producer and engineer based in the Chicago area. The name comes from Polish, where the spoken phrase reads as “it’s just me”. She trained on classical guitar, piano and voice as a child, studied music business and audio engineering at the SAE Institute in 2016, and started the project in 2017 with the single “Funeral For Love”. The debut album “Code Blue” followed on 26 October 2018, self-released, with the single “Farewell – Mirrors Don’t Lie” alongside it. The catalogue after that ran quickly. “Code Blue Reloaded” and “Code Blue Revelations” both landed in 2020, the five-part EP “Out of Order” in 2021 and the acoustic EP “Ghosts” in 2022. “Panic Room” arrived in 2023, produced with Walter Flakus of Stabbing Westward, whose US dates she opened that year. Flakus also worked on the “I am the Fire” EP and the album “DRAMA”, both 2024, the year Side-Line covered her video for ‘Fraud’ and talked to her about the new album. She has been a member of The Joy Thieves since 2019 and toured with Pigface the same year. Remixers and collaborators across the catalogue include Rhys Fulber, who remixed “Flashback” in 2019, Tim Skold, who remixed “Motion” in 2020, and Julian Beeston of Nitzer Ebb, whose “We The People”, “Higher Than The Sun” and “Crazy Horses” all feature her. She has also remixed PIG’s “The New Disorder”. In 2024 she toured the United States with Orgy and Cold and played her first European dates supporting Front Line Assembly, and she returned to Europe in February and March 2026 as direct support on KMFDM’s tour. Femme Fatale Records, her own imprint, has carried her releases since 2024 and now issues “Closer”.
